This bill would provide additional funding to the Australian government for the remainder of the 2017-2018 financial year.

It would appropriate money from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for grants to states, territories and local governments, new programs, non-operating appropriations, and payments to corporate Commonwealth entities.
The bill would also replenish the Advance to the Finance Minister to restore the same level of discretionary appropriation available at the start of the financial year.
Appropriates money from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for specific purposes including grants and new programs.
Replenishes the Advance to the Finance Minister to restore discretionary appropriation levels.
Ensures that appropriations for purposes covered by a Special Account replenish that account by the same amount.
The Australian government, including departments and corporate Commonwealth entities, as well as states, territories and local governments.

Appropriation Bill (No. 6) 2017-2018 seeks just over $6.2 billion, including $6 billion for the Department of the Environment and Energy to purchase the New South Wales and Victorian governments' shares in Snowy Hydro Limited, and $94 million for the Department of Home Affairs to upgrade risk assessment and identity management ICT capabilities.
The speaker announced that unless otherwise ordered, five appropriation bills would be referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration at the adjournment of the House.

The budget delivers tax relief for over 75,000 people in Brisbane, a record $75 billion national infrastructure pipeline with over $20 billion for Queensland projects including the Brisbane Metro, and $1.3 billion for a National Health and Medical Industry Growth Plan, while contrasting Labor’s commitment to retaining a 49 per cent top marginal tax rate.

The speaker announced total appropriations of just under $108.5 billion for the 2018-19 financial year and just under $8 billion in supplementary appropriations, including $6.5 billion for the Department of the Environment and Energy—$6 billion for purchasing New South Wales and Victorian government shares in Snowy Hydro Limited and under $435 million for the Reef 2050 Long Term Sustainability Plan.
